skill.name: writing-plans
skill.description: Creates detailed, test-first implementation plans for multi-step coding work before development begins.
skill.summary: Turn requirements into bite-sized implementation plans with files, tests, commands, and handoff steps.
skill.author: ZhanlinCui

security_audit.summary: All static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline command examples in SKILL.md. The skill is a planning guide for implementation plans. No executable Ruby backticks, hidden command execution, network access, or prompt-injection attempt was found.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 18 is an inline Markdown path template for where to save plan documents. It is not Ruby syntax or an executable shell backtick.
Lines 33-45 are a fenced Markdown template for a plan header. The fence is documentation content and does not execute commands.
Line 45 is the closing delimiter for a Markdown code fence. It has no command execution behavior.
Line 49 opens a fenced Markdown example for task structure. It is formatting syntax, not executable code.
Line 53 wraps an example file path in Markdown inline code. The path is documentation for a plan, not a command.
Line 54 wraps an example file range in Markdown inline code. It describes an edit target and does not invoke a shell.
Line 55 wraps an example test path in Markdown inline code. It is a static path reference, not executable Ruby or shell syntax.
Line 59 opens a fenced Python example inside the plan template. The skill documents sample test structure and does not run the code.
Line 63 is a Markdown code fence delimiter. It is non-executable documentation syntax.
Line 67 shows a pytest command that a plan may ask a developer to run. The skill itself does not execute the command or accept untrusted command input.
Line 72 opens a fenced Python example for minimal implementation. It is illustrative plan content, not runtime code.
Line 75 is a Markdown code fence delimiter. It has no execution semantics.
Line 79 repeats an example pytest command for plan verification. This is a documented instruction for a future workflow, not automatic command execution.
Lines 84-87 are a fenced bash example containing git add and commit commands. The skill only includes them as plan text and does not execute them.
Line 87 is the closing delimiter for a Markdown bash fence. It is formatting syntax and not executable code.
Line 88 closes the larger Markdown task template fence. It does not represent Ruby backtick execution or shell execution.

content.value_statement: Complex coding requests often fail when the next steps are vague. This skill turns requirements into clear plans with files, tests, commands, and execution handoffs.
actual_capabilities: Creates implementation plans saved under a docs/plans date-based filename.
Structures plans with a goal, architecture notes, tech stack, and task sections.
Breaks coding work into small test-first steps for each component.
Lists exact files to create, modify, or test for each task.
Includes expected test commands, expected outcomes, and commit steps.
Offers handoff options for subagent-driven or separate-session execution.
limitations: It writes plans and does not execute the implementation itself.
It depends on accurate requirements and codebase context from the user or agent.
Referenced companion skills may not exist in every environment.
Generated commands still need review before use in a real repository.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Feature
use_cases.description: Convert a feature request into small tasks with tests, file targets, and commit points.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Coding Handoff
use_cases.description: Create a plan that another agent or teammate can follow without prior project context.

use_cases.title: Improve Test Coverage Work
use_cases.description: Break a risky change into failing tests, minimal fixes, verification commands, and review checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Change
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a focused implementation plan.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a small change. Include the goal, files to inspect, files to edit, tests to write, and verification commands.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an implementation plan for this feature. Break the work into bite-sized tasks, include test-first steps, and name the exact files likely to change.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Refactor
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for safer code migration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a refactor plan that preserves behavior. Include characterization tests, incremental edits, risk checks, and commands that confirm each task is complete.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Multi-Agent Execution
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete handoff plan for another agent. Include task order, review checkpoints, expected outputs, commands to run, and the final validation sequence.

output_examples.input: Plan adding password reset to an existing web app.
output: A dated plan file path under docs/plans.
A goal, architecture summary, and key framework notes.
Tasks for tests, token creation, email flow, UI states, verification, and commits.

output_examples.input: Plan a safe migration from one settings module to another.
output: A task list that starts with characterization tests.
Exact modules to inspect and update.
Verification commands and rollback-aware review points.

best_practices: Provide the relevant requirements, constraints, and repository context before asking for a plan.
Ask for exact files, tests, commands, and expected outputs in every task.
Review generated commands and paths before executing them in a repository.
anti_patterns: Do not use it when you want immediate code edits instead of a plan.
Do not accept vague tasks that omit tests, files, or verification steps.
Do not run generated shell commands without checking project-specific risks.

faq.question: Does this skill write code?
faq.answer: It writes implementation plans. The plan may include sample snippets and commands, but execution is a separate step.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it before a multi-step coding task, especially when another person or agent must implement the work.

faq.question: Does it support test-driven development?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill asks for failing tests, minimal implementation, passing test verification, and commits.

faq.question: Can it be used with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Will it execute shell commands?
faq.answer: No. It may place commands in a plan, but users or agents must decide whether to run them.

faq.question: What context should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the feature request, known constraints, relevant paths, testing expectations, and any repository conventions.
